title: Shelfwise Quickstart credits & hosting/privacy evaluation
summary: Initial discovery to understand Shelfwise's quickstart needs. Discussed Redwood free credits path to first token, hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/private deployment constraints (data retention, KMS, SOC2), benchmark plan (latency/cost), and next-step pilot with pricing and a short benchmark run. Agreed to share security pack and pilot SOW. SE to propose sample load and example config for caching/batching.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
Security: SOC2, KMS, retention, audit logs
Pilot scope and benchmarks: latency, cost per 1k tokens, sample dataset
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Diaz (Redwood SE), Ari Patel (CTO, Shelfwise), Leah Kim (PM), Jon Serrano (DevOps)

Summary auto: brief notes captured by system - may be incomplete

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we really appreciate you carving out time. quick intro — I'm Maya, AE, and Carlos is our systems engineer. Ari, Leah, Jon, thanks for being here. Can you do quick intros?
[00:14] Ari (Shelfwise): Yep, sure. I'm Ari — CTO at Shelfwise, we're a small team building a recommendations/search layer for indie bookstores basically. Leah is PM working on features and Jon handles infra.
[00:28] Leah (Shelfwise): Hi all. quick note: timeline is tight, we want to have a pilot in december if possible.
[00:34] Jon (Shelfwise): And we care a lot about data privacy, retention, and keys. we run on AWS, EKS, and would prefer VPC peering or private connectivity if possible.
[00:45] Carlos (Redwood): Got it, thanks. high level today we wanted to walk through the self-serve quickstart path — free credits, time to first token, plus options if you need dedicated capacity or private VPC. Also we can cover security requirements.
[01:00] Ari: perfect. two big questions up front: 1) how fast can we go from sign-up to a simple generation/embedding call? 2) if we need guaranteed throughput or regional hosting, how does that work?
[01:14] Maya: Great. for the first — TTFT — most customers get an initial key and make their first call within an hour, often within 10-20 minutes if they follow the quickstart. we provide code samples, SDKs, and a Postman/CLI flow. we also give an initial free credit bundle for prototyping.
[01:30] Leah: what's the size of that credit bundle? and does it cover embeddings + gen or just tokens?
[01:38] Maya: Typically our quickstart credits cover both. the default package is a $1k equivalent credit for 30 days for qualifying pilots — covers mixed usage. but we can scope smaller for PLG signups. Carlos can speak to example token burn.
[01:55] Carlos: right: for a 10k token/embeddings run the charges vary by model; if you use a smaller open model we show cost estimates in the console. For bench runs we recommend a 1K-5K request sample set to measure latency variance and cost.
[02:12] Jon: ok. on hosting — is the default hosted flow multi-tenant? what data touches Redwood storage?
[02:18] Maya: Hosted is multi-tenant and we keep request logs/metadata for operational purposes by default, retention is configurable. For regulated data or PII you'd want Dedicated or Private. We also offer a Private VPC option where the inference plane sits in your VPC and logs don't leave your network, plus an on-prem appliance option for air-gapped requirements.
[02:40] Ari: we definitely want encryption with our KMS and separation of keys. can you integrate customer-managed KMS?
[02:48] Carlos: yes — KMS integration is part of the private deployment and dedicated options. For hosted, we have an option for customer-managed keys for model storage and at-rest if you need that, but full KMS/HSM integration with audit key policies is usually done for Private deployments.
[03:05] Leah: SOC2 and compliance. do you have SOC2 Type II and do you provide evidence packs?
[03:11] Maya: we are SOC2 Type II and we can supply the attestation and our security questionnaire. we'll send the security pack after call.
[03:20] [Speaker 1]: (mumbled) how about RBAC and SSO?
[03:23] Maya: good q — console supports SAML-based SSO and RBAC granularity; for API keys you can namespace keys per project, and we expose audit logs.
[03:32] Ari: good. let's talk performance — typical p95 latency for short generations, say 256 tokens?
[03:38] Carlos: it depends on model and plan. on Hosted, for verified open models p95 might be 150-400ms per request for small seqs using our optimized runtime. Dedicated reserved pools give lower tail latencies and better throughput. For heavy production we often recommend Dedicated with autoscale policies.
[03:55] Leah: if we start hosted for quick iteration and then move to Dedicated later, how hard is that migration?
[04:02] Maya: designed to be seamless — same API surface, model version pinning, rollout policy. you can pin traffic to dedicated pool once provisioned. Carlos: from infra perspective, we keep the same request/response format and there is a config toggle, so app-level changes are minimal.
[04:18] Jon: what's the lead time for dedicated pools?
[04:21] Carlos: depends on region and capacity — 2-6 weeks typical for reserved capacity. for urgent pilots we can allocate burst capacity or a short-term shared pool.
[04:31] Ari: timeline wise — we want a small benchmark and a pilot by mid-december, can you support that?
[04:36] Maya: yes. propose a pilot: 3 weeks, sample dataset of 5k tokens per request set, run embeddings + generation tests, measure latency and cost. we'll assign credits to cover the bench.
[04:49] Leah: what about logs/PII from test dataset? we can scrub, but for realism we might need small PII-like examples.
[04:57] Carlos: for bench runs we recommend synthetic but realistic-looking data; if you need to run real PII we can do it on Private or Dedicated to satisfy retention.
[05:08] [00:05:10] Ari: okay. can you walk briefly through dev experience — how would our devs test from their laptop?
[05:14] Carlos: sure — typically devs sign up, create an api key in console, then use our SDK to call generate/embeddings. we have a local dev recipe that shows how to mock KV cache and use prefix caching. sample command: rwd-cli invoke --model open-xt-1 --text "...". (note: transcript may mis-hear cli flags)
[05:37] [00:05:37] Jon: what's rate limiting look like? we have spiky traffic from batch jobs during nightly updates.
[05:41] Carlos: we support per-key rate limits and token quotas. Dedicated pools can be configured for steady throughput and burst policies. also recommend batching for batch jobs to reduce cost.
[05:52] Leah: any network setup for VPC? how do we peer?
[05:55] Maya: Private VPC uses a transit/peering connection or AWS PrivateLink depending on region. we'll send a network runbook.
[06:02] Ari: Perfect. can we get a sample SOW or pilot pricing?
[06:06] Maya: absolutely. I'll send pricing tiers and a short pilot SOW.
[06:10] [00:06:10] Speaker 2 (automated): note - "KV cash" logged in transcript
[06:15] Carlos: ha, yeah sometimes the transcript reads KV cash, we mean KV cache.
[06:20] Ari: (laughs) okay. we also wanted to talk about model control — can we bring our own checkpoint or do you only host curated models?
[06:28] Carlos: You can bring-your-own-model for dedicated/private, we also support standard open models in the hosted catalog. For BYO we handle the onboarding and model verification; there's a small review for quantization compatibility and inference kernels.
[06:44] Jon: is the model weight storage encrypted and can we restrict who in our org can deploy?
[06:49] Maya: yes to encryption and we have role restrictions in the console. + audit logs for deployments.
[06:55] Leah: ok so next — evaluation metrics. we want p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and quality on a small eval set. what data and tooling do you need from us?
[07:07] Carlos: sample dataset (we recommend 200-500 prompt pairs for quality eval), seed randomization for bench, and a small N for embeddings similarity checks. we'll provide a bench script and results dashboard.
[07:20] Ari: do you do reranking or suggest a combo of embed+rerank? we're exploring reranking for product search.
[07:26] Carlos: reranking is supported. we often recommend an embeddings + nearest neighbor followed by a lightweight rerank model — that balances latency/cost.
[07:34] [00:07:34] Jon: if we go dedicated, what's SLO and SLA?
[07:38] Maya: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and we can commit to latency targets with agreed scaling rules. we'll include SLA language in pilot SOW for reserved capacity.
[07:48] Leah: quick question on observability — what does console surface?
[07:51] Maya: token-level cost, per-route latency, traces, error rates, and we'll give tracing hooks for distributed traces. you can export logs to your SIEM.
[07:59] Ari: good. security again — we want a paper trail for data access. does the private option integrate with our Okta groups?
[08:06] Carlos: yes SAML + Okta groups mapping for RBAC.
[08:10] [00:08:10] Ari: sweet. are you integrated with typical KMS providers?
[08:13] Maya: yes — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM support for private.
[08:18] Leah: great. timeline — if we sign up now, when do you think we can run a bench?
[08:23] Maya: if you sign up and accept the pilot SOW this week, we can hand out quickstart credits immediately and schedule a bench next week. Carlos: we'll need 1-2 devs from you to run the bench and a short network window for private tests if you go that route.
[08:40] Ari: sounds feasible. budget — any rough numbers for a 3-week pilot?
[08:44] Maya: typical pilot sticker including credits and SE time is about $8-15k depending on scale; we can size it smaller. the free credits we provide usually cover the bench itself.
[08:55] Jon: will we get access to a staging pool that's more similar to production?
[08:58] Carlos: we can allocate a short-lived dedicated pool or a shared high-perf pool for bench. we'll note the configuration in the SOW.
[09:10] Leah: ok can we cover next steps?
[09:12] Maya: sure. recap: 1) we'll send the security pack, pilot SOW, and pricing. 2) Carlos will share bench scripts and sample config for batching/caching. 3) we'll provision quickstart credits upon SOW agreement. 4) schedule bench next week.
[09:28] Ari: can you include a network runbook for VPC peering?
[09:31] Carlos: yes will attach runbook and sample Terraform snippets.
[09:35] [00:09:35] Maya: perfect. any final Qs?
[09:38] Jon: one small thing — do you provide tokenized cost breakdown per model in the console?
[09:41] Maya: yes per-token and per-route breakdowns in console and via API export.
[09:45] Ari: ok thanks — excited to move quickly.
[09:48] Maya: awesome, we'll follow up with docs and SOW. thanks everyone.
